clue.text: Group to assess for a speaker a passage between seats

parts.note: a gang is a group of people

indicators.note: what is meant for a speaker is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to weigh something up is to assess it; said out loud it matches a common word for a route

explanation.surface: A committee meets to judge something on behalf of a public speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: GANG plus a word that sounds like WEIGH gives GANGWAY. 'Group to assess' reads like a panel's job, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is the aisle running between rows of seating, especially in a theatre or the House of Commons.

clue.text: Leading lives essentially shown in place of records

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: The main lives of a biography are kept in a records office.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCH (chief, as in archbishop) plus the core of LIVES gives ARCHIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a repository where historical documents and papers are stored and kept.

clue.text: Information on a category of music?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'
re means about or concerning, as in the subject line of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details about a particular style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN (British slang for information) plus RE (concerning) gives GENRE. 'On' looks like a joining word but supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a style or kind of artistic work, such as jazz, folk or rock in music.

clue.text: Poison spilt in case? About right

indicators.note: about can mean around, so one piece goes around another
something spilt is scattered out of its container, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Poison has leaked inside a container, and someone asks if that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IN CASE into A...SENIC and put it around R. 'In case' looks like a phrase meaning 'just in case', but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notoriously toxic element, long used by poisoners in history and fiction.

clue.text: Protection for the finger or the limb possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several possible forms, so the letters may be put in another order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between guarding just a finger or the whole arm.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LIMB rearranged gives THIMBLE. The word 'or' suggests two alternatives of protection, but it only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a small cap worn on the fingertip to push a needle while sewing without pricking the skin.

clue.text: Very unpleasant mob shortly around Rhode Island

indicators.note: shortly here means in short form, so the word loses its final letter
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a horde is a mob; cut short it drops its last letter
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A nasty crowd quickly gathers in the US state of Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: HORDE without its E goes around RI. 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it trims a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid is a near synonym for nasty or dreadful, describing something extremely disagreeable.

clue.text: Trim men when dancing welcoming outsiders from earlier jollity

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece receives another inside it
dancers move around and change places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its outermost letters, the first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Slim men at a dance greet guests who arrived before them.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIM MEN rearranged into M...RIMENT takes in ER, the outside letters of EARLIER. 'When' is a link word here, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment and jollity are both nouns for cheerful fun, laughter and festive high spirits.

clue.text: See a French and German comfortable outdoor chair

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see, as in 'lo and behold'
un is French for a
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone invites you to look at a French and a German pair of garden chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: LO plus UN plus GER gives LOUNGER. 'A French' asks for the French word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining seat, often with a long footrest, used by pools and in gardens.

clue.text: A preppy tailor dressed in a fitting way

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange or prepare it, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out tailor dresses in clothes that suit him well.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of A PREPPY TAILOR are rearranged. 'Dressed' reads as clothing, fitting the tailor, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriately is an adverb meaning suitably or properly, which matches doing something in a fitting manner.

clue.text: Examine source of contagion in medical facility

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a place for treating the sick

indicators.note: the source of something is where it starts, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Doctors investigate where an infection started inside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside SAN, the short form of sanatorium. 'Source of contagion' sounds like an epidemiology phrase but gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or inspect something closely, a verb close in sense to examine.

clue.text: Top bunch of musicians get drink with Queen and rise round dinner's end

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
to rise is to go up

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A star band, Queen, have a drink and then stand up at the end of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is printed in italics as the rock band, yet it supplies the royal cipher Elizabeth Regina. 'Get' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A supergroup is a band formed of musicians already famous from other successful groups.

clue.text: One serving has disposition to submit

indicators.note: one serving in a unit or household is placed within it, so a piece goes inside another

parts.note: someone given to something has a disposition or tendency towards it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A waiter has the right temperament for being obedient.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits inside GIVEN, as in 'given to anger', meaning inclined. 'One serving' suggests a waiter but is one inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is a phrasal verb meaning to yield or surrender, the same as to submit.

clue.text: Loops put round excellent line in barriers

indicators.note: something put round another encloses it

parts.note: rings are loops
A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the figure 1
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Coils are wrapped round a fine wire inside some fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: RINGS goes around AI plus L. AI stands for A1, top quality, with the digit read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings are fences made of upright bars, used as barriers along roads, stairs and parks.

clue.text: Pose price mistakenly for part of a submarine

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quotes the wrong cost for a component of a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: POSE PRICE rearranged gives PERISCOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A periscope is the tube with mirrors that lets a submerged submarine's crew see above the surface.

clue.text: Varied centres in information technology converge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: IT is the usual abbreviation for information technology

indicators.note: to vary something is to change it, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Different computer hubs come together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' looks like an adjective describing the centres, but it is the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or roads that intersect meet and cross at a point, so they come together or converge.

clue.text: Worries shown by European in distant society

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: far means distant
E is the abbreviation for European
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A European living in a faraway community displays his anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside FAR, then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Fears and worries are both plural nouns for anxious feelings about what might happen.

clue.text: Hackneyed ceremony after last part of Lent

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another in the answer
the last part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A tired old ritual held at the very end of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the last letter of LENT, comes before RITE. Lent is the Christian season before Easter, which suits the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed and trite are both adjectives for remarks or ideas made dull by overuse.

clue.text: Take the place of first woman supporting rector and priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting others sits beneath them, so it comes last

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
Eli is the priest of the Old Testament who raised Samuel
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The leading woman in a parish backs both the rector and the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus ELI, with EVE beneath them in the down light. Eli is a crossword favourite for priest.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take over their duty, as when a sentry is replaced by the next guard.

clue.text: Separation from companion with old cat amid household work

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so pieces sit inside another

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, home repair and improvement work
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
O is the abbreviation for old
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A friend and an elderly cat are split apart in the middle of home renovations.
explanation.walkthrough: Companion of Honour is a British order whose holders put two letters after their names; DIY is do-it-yourself home improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dichotomy is a division into two contrasting parts, so it means a split or separation.

clue.text: Try, for example, to generate rumour

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Someone attempts, as an illustration, to start some gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but here it is the courtroom sense: a judge hears a case. SAY works like 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information passed on from others that cannot be verified, which is what a rumour is.

clue.text: TV chef James has current drink

parts.note: James Martin is a British television chef
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A celebrity cook enjoys a fashionable beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: James Martin is a well-known British television chef; add I, the physics symbol for current. 'Current' looks like 'fashionable' but is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Ceramic item at front of office is thing that's chipped?

parts.note: a pot is a piece of pottery
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A china vase at an office reception desk has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: POT plus AT plus O. A chipped pot fits the ceramic surface, but the definition means cut into chips, the British word for fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes are cut into chips, the British name for French fries, so a potato is what gets chipped.

clue.text: Ticket seller following confused impression gets to speak without thinking?

indicators.note: following places one piece after another in the answer

parts.note: a blur is a hazy, indistinct image
a tout sells tickets unofficially, usually at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A scalper outside a venue, muddled, ends up talking rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the ticket seller first, but 'following' puts it second in the answer. A tout resells tickets, like a scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: To blurt out something is to say it suddenly and tactlessly, without stopping to consider.

clue.text: Promise made by a leader of scouts? Certainly!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
sure! is a casual way of saying certainly

explanation.surface: A scout leader is asked whether he makes a pledge, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus S plus SURE. 'Leader of scouts' looks like a scoutmaster but means only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to tell them confidently that something is so, a verb close to promise or guarantee.

clue.text: Some reversal sadly for Latin American dance music

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the answer is a run of letters within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sad setback for a South American dance band.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits forwards in reverSAL SAdly. 'Reversal' tempts you to read backwards, but it is only part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American style of dance and the music played for it, rooted in Cuban rhythms.

clue.text: Vets eg able to be corrupted? They could be roasted!

indicators.note: something corrupted is altered from its proper form, so the letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Could vets be bribed? If so, they deserve a public roasting!
explanation.walkthrough: VETS EG ABLE rearranged. 'Roasted' looks like harsh criticism of the vets, but the definition means cooked in an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes, parsnips and carrots are commonly roasted, so vegetables are examples of what could be roasted.

clue.text: US city linked to Irish haunt

indicators.note: things linked to each other are joined end to end

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An American city has ties to a favourite Irish hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: LA plus IR gives LAIR. 'Haunt' looks like a ghost's verb but is a noun for a regular hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hideout where a person or animal regularly goes, which is a haunt.

clue.text: Briefly refer to chaps with container containing oxygen

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A quick reference to some men carrying an oxygen cylinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' sounds like a wordplay instruction to shorten something, but it belongs to the definition: to refer briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention something is to speak of it in passing, without going into detail.

clue.text: Lots in police department recalled as enterprising

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
lots means many

explanation.surface: Many officers in a police unit are brought back for showing initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: The Criminal Investigation Department is the detective branch of British police forces; the container is built first, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic and enterprising both describe someone energetic who is full of initiative and drive.
